segments.text: An agent is asked to remove inactive customer accounts. It expects to delete forty-eight rows.

SOUNDING runs that exact deletion in a transaction that can only roll back, and measures what really moved: two hundred and eighty-nine row changes in ten tables. Cascades, broken links, messages to outside providers.
Policy blocks it: unpaid invoices, live subscriptions, records the law says to keep. The agent narrows its own plan from that evidence, and simulates again.
Now it's safe. Approval isn't a yes button: it signs this exact set of effects, with a one-time token that expires in five minutes.
Then the world moves. A customer phones in an order, and I execute anyway. The verifier finds three changes nobody approved.
It rolls back before commit, and proves that every row it touched is intact.
Simulate again, on what is true now. Narrow, approve, execute. Committed, and every check verified.
Even the undo goes through the same gate. Queued messages are cancelled for real; anything already sent is admitted, not hidden.
Across forty seeded scenarios: every committed effect predicted exactly, twenty-five of twenty-five drifts caught, zero unsafe commits.
SOUNDING. See the consequences before they become real.
